newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cartel office rejects Holzmann share pool.
newsitem.headline: German cartel office rejects Holzmann share pool.

text.p: The German Federal Cartel Office said on Tuesday that it rejected the proposal by Deutsche Bank and builder Hochtief AG to pool their shares in Philipp Holzmann AG in a blocking deposit.
In a statement, the watchdog also said that it wanted to regain responsibility for the Holzmann case from the European Commission. The deal is currently subject to EU approval.

"We will request that the European Commission turns responsibility for this case back to the German Federal Cartel Office, because the case needs to be dealt with in the area where it has the greatest impact -- in Germany," it said.

In January 1995 the monopolies watchdog stopped Hochtief upping its stake in Holzmann to 35 percent and said allowing the move would give Hochtief technical, financial and organisational control of the German construction market for large projects.
The president of the Cartel Office, Dieter Wolf, said the share pool involved "serious considerations regarding competition".
The Cartel Office said that the share pool was presented in such a way as to fulfil European Union merger conditions and said that it thought this was an attempt to get around German merger law.
"While the company law aspects of the deal appear to fulfil conditions laid down by Brussels, the dangers to competition in this deal are mostly in the German market," the statement said.
